summary:
Astrea brings real NASA SPHEREx observations into an interactive sky explorer. Users can select a region, inspect infrared images, and build a sequence of observations from different dates. A draggable timeline and adjustable blink playback make it easier to look for possible motion or changes in brightness. An additional spectrum view shows how a selected sky position varies across infrared wavelengths, with measurement uncertainties and quality information.
Built for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, Astrea connects public astronomical data with an accessible experience for curious beginners and astronomy enthusiasts. It combines sky navigation, English and Spanish guidance, and on-demand data retrieval to reduce the technical barriers to exploration. Its goal is to help more people investigate the changing sky and identify observations worth examining further.
details:
Astrea is an interactive web application that makes real SPHEREx observations easier to explore, compare, and understand. It connects a navigable sky view with infrared images from NASA/IPAC’s Infrared Science Archive, bringing astronomical data into an experience designed for curious newcomers and astronomy enthusiasts.

Users select a region directly in the sky or enter its coordinates. They can inspect observations alongside their capture dates, detectors, and source information, adjust image appearance, and access the original scientific FITS files.

The comparison workflow lets users find observations by year and detector, add multiple images to a sequence, and explore them through a draggable timeline or automatic blink playback. Images are positioned using their astronomical coordinates and share a display scale during comparison. This helps users investigate possible movement and changes in brightness.

The Spectrum panel provides another perspective. It measures a fixed sky position across multiple exposures and displays brightness against infrared wavelength. Users can enable different detectors and inspect observation dates, estimated uncertainties, and quality indicators. PSF fitting and aperture photometry provide two measurement approaches.

Accessibility is central to the project. Astrea includes English and Spanish interfaces and an interactive guide using real SPHEREx observations. A sky rendered from the Hipparcos catalogue provides visual context, while detailed processing controls remain optional.

We built the frontend with React and Three.js and the Python backend with FastAPI, Astropy, Astroquery, and NumPy. The backend discovers observations through IRSA’s Simple Image Access service and retrieves selected regions and data planes when needed. Caching reduces repeated downloads.

Our contribution is the combination of sky navigation, temporal comparison, and introductory spectral exploration in one interface. Astrea supports the challenge by making the changing sky easier to investigate. Visual differences remain candidates for further examination: wavelength coverage, image artifacts, and measurement conditions can also affect their appearance.
